landmarks.name: Centre for Athletics, Recreation and Special Abilities
Clearihue Building
facts: It underwent a major $15 million redevelopment in 2013.

landmarks.name: Jamie Cassels Centre
facts: It was called the University Centre until 2020, when it was renamed after a departing president.
The university's art gallery and museum was here until it moved to the main library in 2011.

landmarks.name: McKinnon Building
facts: Its gym was the former home of the Vikes; the basketball court was named after two legendary coaches in 2002.

landmarks.name: Student Union Building
facts: The student society runs it, with free phones, a darkroom and study space.
It was one of the first buildings built on campus.

landmarks.name: Cornett Building
facts: It is a sprawling complex of courts and staircases, home to Anthropology, Psychology and Sociology.

landmarks.name: MacLaurin Building
facts: This modernist complex houses the Faculty of Education, the School of Music and the David Lam Auditorium.

landmarks.name: Petch Building
facts: It houses Biochemistry and Microbiology and the School of Earth and Ocean Sciences.

landmarks.name: Bob Wright Centre
facts: It is home to Chemistry, Earth and Ocean Sciences and the Canadian Centre for Climate Modelling and Analysis.

landmarks.name: Business and Economics Building
facts: It houses the Gustavson School and the offices of senior university administrators.

landmarks.name: First Peoples House
facts: It is a gathering place for Indigenous students, co-designed by Alfred Waugh and Kenneth Wong.

landmarks.name: Halpern Centre for Graduate Students
facts: It houses the student society for master's and PhD students and a restaurant open to the public.

landmarks.name: Mearns Centre for Learning
facts: It is the main library, home to the Special Collections and University Archives.

landmarks.name: University Club
facts: It opened on March 16, 1982, as a dining and meeting place for faculty.

landmarks.name: Roderick Haig-Brown
facts: It is a large residence hall named after a writer and conservationist who worked to protect the Fraser River.

landmarks.name: Arthur Currie
facts: It is an on-campus residence named after the general who commanded the Canadian Corps in the First World War.
